newsitem.title: JORDAN: Amman stocks drop below key 160-point level.
newsitem.headline: Amman stocks drop below key 160-point level.

text.p: Jordan's stock market dipped below the 160-point psychological barrier on Saturday but investor optimism of a resumed buying spree by global funds buttressed overall trade, dealers said.
The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index shed 0.46 percent to close at 159.60 points in moderate turnover worth 1.42 million dinars ($2 million).
Since last Sunday the market has lost the momentum following two weeks of buying by global funds focused primarily on mining blue-chip stocks and cement.
The retreat by foreign funds erased some of the gains which sent prices to their highest levels in nearly two years.
But brokers expect the market to pick up later in the week after global funds resume purchases on attractively priced blue-chips.

"Orders by foreign funds are expected to resume on Monday," said Nasser al-Amad, head of United Financial Investments, adding the market was generally stable and attributing the recent drop to profit-taking.
"The recent extraordinary trading by foreigners shows a high demand which is not expected to be short term," Mohammed Abdullah, senior analyst at Pearl Consulting.
Bourse activity was underpinned by a handful of select stocks including Jordan-Kuwait Bank, which rose 4.03 percent to 3.10 dinars on expectations of a bonus share, brokers said.
But Jordan Cement, which spearheaded the market bull run, was unchanged at 4.10 dinars in moderate trade worth 267,030 dinars.
Also unchanged was majority state owned Jordan Phosphate Mines which stood at 3.90 dinars in one of the busiest deals of the day.
Overall falling shares outnumbered gainers by 21 to 13 while another 12 traded but closed unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance shed 0.08 percent to 80.87 points, 3.03 percent down from the start of the year.
